_comment: Detector thresholds. Every number here is a tuning decision, not a law of
nature. DETECTIONS.md explains why each value was chosen and what happens
when you move it. Thresholds were tuned against the synthetic dataset

profiling._comment: Baselines are built ONLY from the attack-free training window.

_comment: Alerts are grouped into an incident when they share an entity (account
or source IP) and are close in time. window_minutes is the maximum gap
between two alerts for them to be linked.

brute_force._comment: 8 failures from ONE IP against ONE account inside 5 minutes.

password_spray._comment: One source, many accounts, few tries each: low-and-slow.

credential_stuffing._comment: Many sources converging on ONE account: distributed guessing.

_comment: 900 km/h is roughly commercial cruising speed. min_distance_km avoids
firing on GeoIP jitter between nearby cities.
Fires when a successful login lands inside the account's longest
dormant stretch (its 'night'), shrunk by neighbour_hours at each end.
Accounts whose dormant stretch is shorter than min_quiet_hours are
skipped: they have no meaningful off-hours to be outside of.

new_device_location._comment: First-ever device fingerprint or country for an established user.

_comment: Burst of failures immediately followed by a success: the classic
shape of a successful account takeover. Critical because, unlike a
bare brute force, the attacker may already be inside.
